name: Scandinavian Defense
description: Hit e4 on move one with 1…d5, then a solid …c6 and …Bf5 set-up.

lines.name: 7.O-O

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 gives the queen a retreat and stops Nb5 or Bb5 tricks.
notes.11: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before …e6.
notes.13: …e6 completes a solid pawn chain and opens the f8 bishop.

lines.summary: Queen to a5, then …Nf6, …c6, …Bf5 and …e6: a Caro-Kann set-up with the queen out.

lines.name: 7.O-O e6 8.Re1

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 gives the queen a retreat and stops Nb5 or Bb5 tricks.
notes.11: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before …e6.
notes.13: …e6 completes a solid pawn chain and opens the f8 bishop.

lines.summary: Against Re1, keep developing with …Nbd7 and …Be7, then castle short.

lines.name: 7.Bd2

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 gives the queen a retreat and stops Nb5 or Bb5 tricks.
notes.11: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before …e6.
notes.13: …e6 completes the pawn chain and opens the f8 bishop.

lines.summary: Against 7.Bd2, play …e6 and watch for the Nd5 trick on your queen.

lines.name: 7.Bd2 e6 8.O-O

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 gives the queen a retreat and stops Nb5 or Bb5 tricks.
notes.11: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before …e6.
notes.13: …e6 completes the pawn chain and opens the f8 bishop.
notes.15: …Nbd7 develops and keeps …Qc7 or …Bb4 for later.

lines.summary: Finish development with …Nbd7, then …Be7 or …Bb4 and castle.

lines.name: 8.Nd5 trick

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 gives the queen a retreat and stops Nb5 or Bb5 tricks.
notes.11: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before …e6.
notes.13: …e6 completes the pawn chain and opens the f8 bishop.
notes.14: Nd5 discovers an attack from the d2 bishop on the a5 queen.
notes.15: …Qd8 is the safe retreat; taking with …cxd5 or …exd5 loses to Bxa5.

lines.summary: When Nd5 uncovers Bd2 on your queen, retreat with …Qd8; never capture the knight.

lines.name: 7.Ne5

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 gives the queen a retreat and stops Nb5 or Bb5 tricks.
notes.11: …Bf5 develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before …e6.
notes.13: …e6 makes room for the bishop and opens the f8 bishop.
notes.15: …Bg6 keeps the bishop; White attacks it with the h-pawn next.
notes.17: …Nbd7 challenges the strong e5 knight so that h5 can be met calmly.

lines.summary: Against Ne5 and the g4/h4 pawn storm, challenge the e5 knight with …Nbd7.

lines.name: 6.Bd2

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 gives the queen a retreat and stops Nb5 or Bb5 tricks.
notes.11: …Bf5: the same set-up; Bc4 and …e6 usually follow.

lines.summary: The order of White's moves doesn't matter: …c6, …Bf5 and …e6 every time.

lines.name: 5.Bd2

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 makes room for the queen, because Bd2 now eyes a5 through the c3 knight.
notes.11: …Bf5 develops; this is the main-line set-up again.

9.Nc6: Bb5! pins the knight and your queen runs short of squares.

lines.summary: Against 5.Bd2, play …c6 at once, because the bishop can now hit your queen through the c3 knight.

lines.name: 5.Bd2 c6 6.Ne4

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.9: …c6 makes room for the queen, because Bd2 now eyes a5 through the c3 knight.
notes.10: Ne4 uncovers the d2 bishop on the a5 queen and attacks f6.
notes.11: …Qd8 is the safe retreat; from d8 the queen also defends f6.
notes.13: …exf6 opens the e-file and the f8 bishop's diagonal.

9.Nc6: Bb5! pins the knight and your queen runs short of squares.

lines.summary: When the knight jumps to e4, retreat the queen to d8 and take back on f6 with the e-pawn.

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.7: …Nf6: the usual move, whatever White's order.
notes.9: …c6: the position is now the same as the main line.

lines.name: 4.Nf3 Nf6 5.Bc4

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Qa5 steps out of the knight's attack; once White plays d4, it pins the c3 knight to the king.
notes.7: …Nf6: the usual move, whatever White's order.
notes.9: …c6 gives the queen a retreat and blunts the c4 bishop's path to b5.

lines.summary: When White skips d4, the same set-up works: …c6, …Bf5 and …e6.

lines.name: 3.d4

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Nf6 develops; the queen is safe on d5 for now.
notes.13: …Qd8 retreats home when c4 hits the queen; the position is solid.
notes.15: …Be7 develops and gets ready to castle.

lines.summary: Same set-up without Nc3: …Nf6, …Bf5, …e6, …c6, and retreat the queen to d8 when kicked.

lines.name: 3.Nf3

notes.1: …d5 challenges e4 at once, so White has no time to build a big centre.
notes.5: …Nf6 develops; after d4 this is the same as the 3.d4 line.
notes.7: …Bf5: the position is now identical to 3.d4 Nf6 4.Nf3 Bf5.

lines.summary: 3.Nf3 and 3.d4 lead to the same position: one plan for both.
